context.note: The work order's references were narrowed against the authorized paths when it was authorized, and the profile's ceiling bounds how many further capsules the assembler may add. `refs` is what the packet actually carries - there is no wider set behind it and no scoped list beside it.

advisory_only: max_turns: no backend this company drives accepts a turn ceiling
company_enforces: developer_attempts: the job state machine refuses a further attempt
context_refs: the packet is built from the narrowed set
enforcement.note: Company OS does not start a process and therefore enforces nothing inside a session. What it can do is refuse to issue the next one.
runner_enforces: wall_seconds: the runner terminates the session process
session_cost: passed to the backend when the backend accepts one

resource_ceiling.escalation_message: Stop and report progress rather than exceeding these ceilings. An honest partial result with a checkpoint is cheaper than a complete one that ran out of budget.

efficiency.strategy_reason: reasoning class C at risk low is routine implementation; profile consumer runs it at the standard tier; evidence is required and affects review depth, not model tier

packet.objective: EngineeringResult.from_mapping defaults the new developer_attempts_remaining field to 0 when the field is absent from an older serialized record (company/engineering/result.py). A zero here is read on the CEO page as "no developer attempts remain", but for a legacy record it actually means the field did not exist yet when the record was written, so the two states are indistinguishable and a CEO could mistakenly treat an unfinished job as exhausted. Change the default for a missing developer_attempts_remaining key so a legacy record is distinguishable from a genuine zero (for example, default to None and render it as unknown rather than a confident 0 on the CEO page's text rendering), without changing the meaning or representation of the field for any record that already carries it.
